extracted.intended_audience: professional communicators (IABC members and business communicators)
extracted.subtask_description: A short code of ethics for professional communicators describing the principles and behaviours expected of IABC members when producing communications (e.g., press releases, corporate messaging). Emphasizes legality, ethics, taste, truthfulness, cultural sensitivity, and ongoing professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge social responsibility and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: As a professional communicator, you have the potential to influence economies and affect lives. This power carries with it significant responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that hundreds of thousands of business communicators worldwide engage in activities that affect the lives of millions of people; therefore communications professionals must be mindful of the social responsibilities their work entails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional communication is legal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is based on principles that assume just societies are governed by a profound respect for human rights and the rule of law. Communications must comply with applicable laws and legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional communication is ethical
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics are the criteria for determining what is right and wrong and can be agreed upon by members of an organization. Communicators should apply agreed ethical standards when creating and distributing messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional communication is in good taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communication is in good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding matters of taste requires sensitivity to cultural norms. Communications should avoid content that is offensive or insensitive to cultural values and beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate with legal, ethical, and cultural sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in communication that is not only legal but also ethical and sensitive to cultural values and beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond mere legal compliance, communicators should evaluate messaging for ethical implications and cultural appropriateness; consider diverse audiences and potential impacts on communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate truthfully, accurately and fairly
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in truthful, accurate and fair communication that facilitates respect and mutual understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure factual accuracy, avoid misleading statements, present information fairly, and craft messages that promote respect and mutual understanding among stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the IABC Code of Ethics articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the principles outlined in the articles of the IABC Code of Ethics for Professional Communicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific articles and provisions of the IABC Code as the authoritative source of ethical rules and standards for professional communicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to continuous competence and knowledge growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Since conditions in the field of communications are always changing, members of IABC will work to improve their individual competence and to increase the body of knowledge through research and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in ongoing professional development, education, and research to maintain and enhance skills and contribute to the wider communications profession's knowledge base.
